questions.hint: A prism has two identical parallel polygon ends and flat rectangular sides (all faces are flat). A cylinder has two flat circular ends and one curved wall.

keyPoints.text: all the prisms
keyPoints.note: Prisms have only flat faces: two identical parallel polygon bases and rectangular side faces.

keyPoints.text: all the cylinders
keyPoints.note: Cylinders have two flat circular ends connected by one curved surface.

questions.solution: The \(7\) prisms (coloured blue) are the Fruit Juice carton, Toy Box, Die (cube), Drawer tray, Tent, Triangular prism block, and Matchbox. The \(4\) cylinders (ticked) are the Jam tin, Birthday cake, Toilet paper roll, and Tall plain cylinder. The Cricket ball (sphere), Hexagonal pyramid, and Ice-cream cone are left unmarked.

steps.explain: Recall the difference between a prism and a cylinder: a prism has two identical polygon bases and flat rectangular sides (like the Fruit Juice carton in blue), while a cylinder has two circular ends and a curved wall (like the Jam tin in yellow).
steps.work: \(\text{Prism: flat polygon faces only},\quad \text{Cylinder: } 2\text{ circular ends} + 1\text{ curved surface}\)

keyPoints.text: classroom objects into prisms and cylinders
keyPoints.note: Books and tissue boxes have 6 flat rectangular faces (prisms); glue sticks and round pencil tins have 2 circular ends and a curved surface (cylinders).

questions.solution: A hardcover book and a tissue box are rectangular prisms (6 flat rectangular faces), while a glue stick and a round pencil tin are cylinders (2 flat circular ends and 1 curved surface).

keyPoints.text: matches the 6th (bottom) 3D object on the left
keyPoints.note: Check the shape of the two parallel end faces and count the side faces on the 6th (bottom) 3D object on the left, then count down the rows on the right from Row 1 to Row 6.

questions.solution: The cylinder (bottom object) has 2 circular end faces and 1 curved surface that unrolls into a rectangle (\(2 + 1 = 3\) faces in total), which matches Row 6: 2 circles and 1 curved rectangular surface.

steps.explain: Locate the 6th (bottom) 3D object on the left (which is a cylinder) and inspect its two parallel end faces (highlighted in yellow): it has 2 circular end faces.

questions.hint: A face is a flat (or curved) surface, an edge is a line where two faces meet, and a corner is a point where edges meet.

keyPoints.text: words face, corner or edge to correctly label each set of arrows
keyPoints.note: A corner is a point where lines meet; an edge is a straight or curved line where two faces meet; a face is a surface.

questions.solution: In b, the arrows from top to bottom point to: Arrow 1: corner, Arrow 2: face, Arrow 3: corner.

steps.explain: Look at Arrow 1 at the top: it points directly to a vertex where three edges meet at a point, which is a corner.

questions.hint: A face is a flat (or curved) surface, an edge is a line where two faces meet, and a corner is a point where edges meet.

keyPoints.text: words face, corner or edge to correctly label each set of arrows
keyPoints.note: A corner is a point where lines meet; an edge is a straight or curved line where two faces meet; a face is a surface.

questions.solution: In f, the arrows from top to bottom point to: Arrow 1: edge, Arrow 2: face, Arrow 3: corner.

steps.explain: Look at Arrow 1 on the triangular prism: it points to the straight sloped line where the triangular front meets the rectangular side, which is an edge.
